prompt: In 120 to 180 words, explain why accuracy can be misleading in exactly five numbered points. Include two alternative metrics and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.user_message: In 120 to 180 words, explain why accuracy can be misleading in exactly five numbered points. Include two alternative metrics and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.
turns.assistant_message: Accuracy can be misleading for several reasons, especially in imbalanced or complex datasets. First, it ignores class distribution — high accuracy may simply reflect predicting the majority class. Second, it treats all errors equally, failing to distinguish between costly false positives and false negatives. Third, accuracy provides no insight into model confidence or calibration. Fourth, it can be inflated by overfitting to noise in the training data. Fifth, accuracy alone doesn’t reveal performance across subgroups, potentially masking disparities. Two alternative metrics are F1-score, which balances precision and recall, and AUC-ROC, which evaluates ranking ability across thresholds. These offer a more nuanced view of model behavior. Ultimately, relying solely on accuracy risks overlooking critical flaws in real-world applications.
